Protecting Our Rivers: From Invisible
Toxins to Quantum Tech
Using atomic-scale Nitrogen-Vacancy centers & Quantum Dots to detect heavy metal
ions in real time—with MOFs for bulk cleanup.
WORLD RIVERS DAY EDUCATIONAL OUTREACH
#WorldRiversDay
01 / The Invisible Threat
What Is Hiding in Clear River Water?
Clear Does Not Mean Clean
Sparkling river water can conceal lethal
concentrations of heavy metal ions from e-waste
and industrial discharge.
Toxic Heavy Metal Culprits
Lead (Pb2+), Mercury (Hg2+), and Cadmium
(Cd2+). They never break down naturally and
accumulate up the food chain.
02 / Current Limits
Why Traditional Water Tests Fall Short
Too Slow
Standard laboratory analysis
takes days or weeks. Pollution
spreads downstream long
before results return.
Low Sensitivity
Field test strips miss ultra-low
concentrations that quietly
build up in fish and human
organs.
The Quantum Goal
Instant, single-molecule
detection deployed on portable
handheld devices right at the
riverbank.
03 / Core Physics
What Is Quantum Sensing?
Smoke Detectors detection a amoke .
A SIMPLE ANALOGY
Imagine a security alarm that detects when someone enters a
room.
A quantum sensor works in a similar way: it uses the special
properties of tiny particles to detect changes in its
surroundings.
Atomic Sensitivity
Quantum sensors exploit the quantum states of single
electrons. When a heavy metal ion approaches, it subtly
alters the magnetic, electric, or optical properties of those
electrons.
04 / Quantum Tool #1
Diamond Defects: Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) Centers
What Is an NV Center?
Pluck out one Carbon atom inside a diamond
lattice and place a Nitrogen atom next to the
empty space (Vacancy). That defect forms an
NV center.
How It Works visually:
Shine a green laser onto the nanodiamond → It
emits a bright red glow. When toxic heavy metals
enter its vicinity, the intensity or frequency of that
red glow instantly changes!
05 / NV Process Flow
How NV Centers Detect Heavy Metals Step-by-Step
Atomic Security Camera: Detects contamination down to single-digit parts-per-billion (ppb) in real time!
1
Pollutant Approach
Lead (Pb2+) or Mercury (Hg2+) ions
float near the diamond surface.
2
Magnetic Field Shift
The metal ion exerts microscopic
magnetic & electric field shifts on
electron spins.
3
Optical Readout
The NV center glow dims or shifts
frequency. Detectors record
concentration instantly.
06 / Quantum Tool #2
Glowing Nanocrystals: Quantum Dots
A quantum dot is a tiny crystal made from
semiconductor materials. When light shines on it, it
can emit light of a particular colour.
Quantum Confinement Effect
Scientists can design its surface to interact with
substances such as lead or mercury. That interaction
can change the light it emits, for example, making it
dimmer.
07 / Quantum Dot Mechanism
Visual Chemical Lock & Key
1. Functional Ligands
Engineers attach
molecular coating on the
dot surface that
specifically grab lead or
mercury ions.
2. Light Quenching
When the metal locks on,
electron transfer quenches
the fluorescence—the glow
turns off completely.
3. Instant Field Readout
Shine a portable UV
flashlight on a water sample;
color shifts instantly reveal
metal presence.
08 / The Comparative Framework
The Molecular Sponge: What Are MOFs?
MOF = Metal-Organic Framework. Tiny
3D porous crystalline structures built like
microscopic cages or scaffolding.
Internal Surface Area
Just 1 gram of a MOF material has an internal
surface area that could cover an entire soccer field!
09 / MOF Action
How MOFs Trap Pollution in Bulk
Porous Trapping
Heavy metal ions flow into
internal cage channels and
get chemically bound inside.
Bulk Filtration
Ideal for water treatment
facilities processing thousands
of gallons per hour.
Reusability
MOFs can be reused
multiple times.
10 / Technology Synergy
Quantum Sensors vs. MOFs: Brain vs. Muscle
+
Quantum Sensors = The Brain & Eyes
Real-time detection. Finds single toxic
molecules instantly and maps exact river
contamination zones.
MOFs = The Muscle
Bulk cleanup. Acts as microscopic sponges
to trap and remove high volumes of
pollution from water.
